recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中成群的漿細胞：核偏心、藍色豐富細胞質與核旁淡染區（hof），並可見雙核及較大核的不成熟漿細胞，提示多發性骨髓瘤。
features: Eccentric round nuclei with clock-face to coarsely clumped chromatin
Abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm with perinuclear hof
Binucleate and larger immature-appearing plasma cells with higher N:C ratio
Background erythrocytes with rouleaux-like stacking and scattered small mature lymphoid/erythroid nuclei
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows numerous plasma cells, some in small clusters. Many are atypical, with binucleation, enlarged nuclei and variation in size, while retaining eccentric nuclei, basophilic cytoplasm and perinuclear clearing. Red cells in the background show a tendency to stack. A precise plasma cell percentage cannot be derived from this single field. Findings are consistent with a plasma cell neoplasm, compatible with multiple myeloma in the proper clinical and laboratory context.

ddx.vs: Reactive plasma cells are mature, usually under 10% of marrow cells, lack binucleation clusters and are polytypic for kappa/lambda.
LPL shows a spectrum of small lymphocytes, plasmacytoid lymphocytes and plasma cells with MYD88 L265P and an IgM paraprotein.
Osteoblasts are larger, occur in cohesive groups and have a pale hof located away from the nucleus rather than directly adjacent to it.
Plasmablastic lymphoma cells are large immunoblast-like cells with prominent central nucleoli, often EBER-positive and typically extramedullary.
